method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name, import slot and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts about script descriptors and call shapes come from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts, read by a bytecode parser, and from the tracked call-site index named in each fact. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the debug console and CommandDebugger natives and of the neighbouring natives that the commanddebugger and system script areas call: the sixteen Debug class natives that no earlier record covers (_printWarning, _getClassName, _getAllCharacter, _getLowResolutionTime, _commandDebug, _getText, _printText, _getTimeCost, _getEventPriority, _getCharacterLocation, _getPlayingCutSceneActor, _deleteQuestActorForPreview, _copyClipboard, _getSpreadSheetAllAttribute, _isSpreadSheetExistAttribute and _getAllItem), the two seeded Math natives, the four position and group natives that scripts call under alias names (_setPos, _setDir, _setPosDirInn and _getAllExtendedTemporaryGroup), _getMemberLocation and six _getSubStat natives. The record also settles that the five names _setDir, _setPos, _setPosDirInn, _callServerOnCommand_cpp and _getAllExtendedTemporaryGroup are not registered literals. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish debug console presentation, server commands or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.MEASURED: Counted or parsed by the method named in the fact, from the executable, from the tracked call-site index or from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/binding_map_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/tutorial_control_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling, the holder receiver adapter, the world object chain and the yield request.

typeRegistry.entries: Entries 0 to 13 are int, float, bool, Utf8String, LuaControl*, AutoReleaseTentative, Nil, Table, IndividualIndex, Variable, LuaControlArray, LuaManyTentativeControlArray, IntegerArray and VariantVectorArray. The constructor stores the StackOperator vftables 0x0110DF38 to 0x0110E140 in steps of 0x28. Earlier records list entries 0 to 9.

dispatch.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller.

framework.holdersNote: The invoke routines cast the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. The Debug holder checks Debug, so a Debug native runs only when the receiver is a Debug control. A null cast returns false without calling the callback.

argumentReaders.0x0071BEB0: LuaControl*, cell tag 4, no class cast.
argumentReaders.0x0071BB80: LuaControl* cast to ActorBase, tag 4 (type descriptor 0x01270964).
argumentReaders.0x0071BC90: LuaControl* cast to CharaBase, tag 4 (type descriptor 0x012709A4).
argumentReaders.0x0071BDA0: LuaControl* cast to PlayerBase, tag 4 (type descriptor 0x012BFA48).
argumentReaders.0x0071BF70: LuaControl* cast to QuestBase, tag 4 (type descriptor 0x012C09A8).
argumentReaders.0x0071C080: LuaControl* cast to SpreadSheet, tag 4 (type descriptor 0x012C2308).

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R] and Y = [X +0x04], the chain of the scheduler contract.

fields.Y +0x0DC: Object that the text natives _getText and _printText call.
fields.Y +0x0E4: Group registry object of the group list helper 0x00701250.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

scriptReceivers.debug: The shipped scripts call the Debug natives as debug:_name(...) on the global debug object (local scan of the sites of _getClassName, _getAllCharacter, _getLowResolutionTime, _commandDebug, _getText, _printText, _getCharacterLocation, _getPlayingCutSceneActor and _copyClipboard). system/debug_u assigns descriptors only for _getClassName, _getAllCharacter, _commandDebug and _getAllItem and a plain function for _getInstanceName.
scriptReceivers.math: The shipped scripts call the seeded integer native as math:_randomIntegerWithSeed(...) on the global math object. system/math_u assigns the descriptors _randomIntegerWithSeed_inl and _randomFloatWithSeed_inl.
scriptReceivers.tier: MEASURED for the descriptor assignments, INFERRED for the receivers and the call shapes.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and writes it to the client log with the kind 0x1F and the prefix <debug>. The callback is a jump to the callback of the Debug registration of _printLog, so the two natives behave identically. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the single instruction 'jmp 0x006E7AB0'. 0x006E7AB0 is the callback that the scheduler contract records for the Debug registration of _printLog.
The Debug registrars of _printLog (0x007363F0) and _printWarning (0x00736540) declare the same lists, none and one Utf8String, and the same wrapper 0x00726930.
The shared callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70, builds the literal <debug> at 0x00FD46D4 and calls 0x0075D4C0 with the engine handle, the kind 0x1F, that string, the text and a zero flag.
The Lua name and its registered name occur in no script of the installed client. The index lists no reference, so the native is engine only.
Whether any engine path or tool calls the Lua name, and why the client registers two names for one callback.

corpusCallSites.sitesNote: The index lists no reference to this Lua name.

arguments.note: The control whose class name is returned.

returns.note: The class record name, or Player in place of MyPlayer.

rows.behavior: Takes a control and pushes the name stored in the class record that its registration record links. The fixed name MyPlayer is replaced by Player. It reads no state beyond the registration record and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the inert helper 0x0078B8E0 on the stack, calls the body 0x0078C3C0 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and the flag 1, and destroys the helper through 0x0078B8F0.
The body tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 through the control reader 0x0071BEB0 and calls 0x00CC7560 on the engine handle with that control.

0x00CC7560 finds the registration record through 0x00CD7A30, calls 0x00CC6FA0 on it and copies the string that 0x00CD2A30 returns. 0x00CC6FA0 copies the string at +0x50 of the record linked at record +0x0C and yields an empty string when that link is null.

With the flag nonzero, which this callback always passes, the body compares the name with the literal MyPlayer at 0x00FE0494 through 0x00445D20. On a match it pushes the literal Player at 0x00FE04A0. Otherwise it pushes the name. Both pushes use 0x007487C0.

The record linked at +0x0C is the class record and the string at +0x50 is its name. The shared field at +0x50 is the one that _getInstanceName reads from the registration record of the control itself. Only the field is stated by the bytes.

The shipped scripts contain 11 call sites in 3 chunks (commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev, system/debug, system/debug_utility). system/debug_u assigns the descriptor _getClassName_inl that returns the pair self and _getClassName_cpp.
All 11 sites are debug:_getClassName(object) calls on the global debug object with one argument, ten with one result used and one with the result returned (local scan).
Which classes carry the names that scripts compare with the result.

arguments.note: Class name, matched against four fixed names and otherwise by a named predicate.

returns.pusher: 0x00748B30 per element after 0x00584F70 for the count

rows.behavior: Takes a class name and pushes the controls of that class from the engine registry. Controls whose instance name starts with __debug are left out. The count is pushed first and then each control, the layout of a LuaControlArray. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 as a Utf8String through 0x0071CE70 after a size test and compares it in order with ActorBaseClass (0x00FD46DC), CharaBaseClass (0x00FD46EC), PlayerBaseClass (0x00FD46FC) and NpcBaseClass (0x00FD470C) through 0x00445D60.

Each branch allocates an 8 byte wrapper and constructs it with 0x00719D70, 0x00719DF0, 0x00719E70, 0x00719EF0 for the four names or 0x0071B2A0 for any other string. The four constructors allocate a 4 byte inner object and build it with 0x00718070, 0x007180D0, 0x00718130 or 0x00718190. 0x0071B2A0 allocates 0x5C bytes and builds a named inner object with 0x00718980 from the engine handle and the string. The callback hands the wrapper to the body through 0x0071B6C0.
The body 0x0078C620 enumerates every control handle with 0x00CC88D0 and keeps a handle when 0x00CC72A0 holds, 0x00CC7310 does not hold and virtual slot 1 of the predicate accepts it.

A kept handle is also required to have an instance name shorter than 7 characters or one whose first 7 characters differ from the literal __debug at 0x00FE04A8. The name comes from 0x00CC7520 and the comparison from 0x00448030.

The body pushes the element count through the int pusher 0x00584F70 and then each handle through the control pusher 0x00748B30. The LuaControlArray push slot builds one table from the count and that many controls, as recorded for _getAllGroup in the chara world contracts.

The predicates are class membership tests. Only their construction is stated here. The names of the four fixed classes and the shape of the named predicate come from the literals and the constructor arguments.

The shipped scripts contain 17 call sites in 4 chunks (commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev, commanddebugger/commanddebuggergm, debug/overloadmonitor, system/debug_utility). system/debug_u assigns the descriptor _getAllCharacter_inl.
All 17 sites are debug:_getAllCharacter(name) calls on the global debug object with one argument and one result (local scan).
The bodies of the predicate virtual slots, the meaning of the flag tested by 0x00CC7310 and the contents of the engine registry that 0x00CC88D0 enumerates.

returns.note: The counter in units of 1000000 per unit.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and pushes one float, the unsigned 64 bit counter at +0x08 of the object that engine implementation +0x184 points to, divided by 1000000.0. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the inert helper, calls the body 0x0078CA80 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and destroys the helper.

The body takes the engine handle from ExecuteParameters +0x04, calls 0x00CC7B20 and reads the qword at the returned address. 0x00CC7B20 loads the engine implementation and returns the pointer stored at its +0x184 plus 8.

Two FILD loads rebuild the value as unsigned. The first loads the low dword and the high dword with the top bit cleared, the second loads the top bit alone and is negated and added. The sum is divided by the double 1000000.0 at 0x00F909C8, stored as a 32 bit float and pushed through 0x007489D0.
The counter counts microseconds and the result is in seconds. The divisor is stated, the unit of the counter is not.

The shipped scripts contain 7 call sites in 3 chunks (commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev, debug/overloadmonitor, widget/debugdispwidget). No script descriptor targets the registered name. system/debug_u has none.
Six sites are debug:_getLowResolutionTime() calls with no argument and one result and one is a string constant (local scan).

The writer and clock of the qword at +0x08 of the object that engine implementation +0x184 points to, and whether the plain Lua name resolves to the registered closure, which the binding map contract stores under _getLowResolutionTime_cpp.

arguments.note: The control whose identity names the debug object.
Selector. dev, gm, test, func or prog.

rows.behavior: Takes a player control, a selector string and optional values. For the selectors dev, gm, test and func it resolves a named debug object for the control and calls its _onCommand Lua function with the values. The selector prog calls a separate routine instead. It pushes the results of _onCommand and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the PlayerBase cast reader 0x0071BDA0 and cell 1 as a Utf8String. The return list builder is 0x00728AC0 and the argument list builder 0x0073D320 declares the registry entries 4, 3 and 9.
The selector is compared in order with dev (0x00FD471C), gm (0x00FD4720), test (0x00FD4724), func (0x00FD472C) and prog (0x00FD4734) through 0x00445D60.

For dev, gm and test the callback converts the control to its binding reference through 0x00CC73B0, formats the instance name _comdebDEV%08X (0x00FE04B0), _comdebGM%08X (0x00FE04C0) or _comdebTEST%08X (0x00FE04D0) with the first dword of that reference through 0x0078B910, 0x0078B9B0 or 0x0078BA50 and looks the name up with 0x00CC7A00, whose catalog name is the lookup that creates the entry.

For func the name is _comdebFUNC%08X (0x00FE04E0) through 0x0078BAF0 and the lookup is 0x00CC7A20, which does not create. When it finds nothing the callback pushes Nil through 0x00748920, pushes the selector string through 0x007487C0 and returns without a call.

When an object was resolved and the call has at least three cells, the callback builds an argument list from the cells from index 2 on through 0x00753B90, 0x0078FAB0 and 0x00791030, unless the call has exactly three cells and the third has the tag 6. It then builds the string _onCommand (0x00FD473C), calls 0x00CD25C0 with the engine handle, the object and the list and publishes the results through 0x00CCA950.
The selector prog calls 0x006FCB80 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and the handle and never builds or calls _onCommand.
The four prefixes name debug command groups. The bytes state the formats and the lookups. The classes of the looked up objects are not stated.

The shipped scripts contain 8 call sites in 5 chunks (chara/npc/debug/populacemenuman, command/debuginputcommand, commanddebugger/commanddebuggerbaseclass, commanddebugger/commanddebuggergm, system/debug_utility). system/debug_u assigns the descriptor _commandDebug_inl.
Seven sites are debug:_commandDebug(...) calls on the global debug object, five with 4 to 7 explicit values and two with an open list, and one is a string constant (local scan).
The bodies of 0x006FCB80, 0x00CC7A00 and 0x00CD25C0, which scripts create the objects named _comdeb..., and the results that a missing object or a failed _onCommand call leaves.

rows.behavior: Takes an actor control, an int and optional values and pushes one Utf8String produced by the text module of the world object. The routine that produces the string contains a yield request, so the call can suspend.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the ActorBase cast reader 0x0071BB80 and cell 1 as an int through 0x005819A0, each after a size test. The argument list builder 0x0073D460 declares the registry entries 4, 0 and 9 and the return list builder is 0x0072B5B0.

It takes the world object through 0x00CC7510 and loads the dword at Y +0x0DC. It collects the cells from index 2 on into a list with 0x007702C0 and builds a default record with 0x006BF420, whose dword at +0x00 is -1 and whose string at +0x04 is empty.
It calls 0x00773B00 on the Y +0x0DC object with the ExecuteParameters pointer, the default record, the control, the int and the list. That routine pushes the result Utf8String through 0x007487C0.
0x00773B00 calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 on a path that does not return the text at once.

The routine formats a text by id and arguments for the actor. The Y +0x0DC object is the one that the display name macro of _getLocalizedDisplayNameForChat uses. Only the reuse of the pointer is stated here.
The shipped scripts contain 2 call sites in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for the name.
Both sites are debug:_getText(...) calls on the global debug object that return the result, one with two explicit arguments and one with an open list (local scan).
The condition of the yield, the lookup source of the text, the formatting rules and the result for an id without text.

arguments.note: Actor control cast to ActorBase, resolved to a handle through 0x00CC73B0.

rows.behavior: Takes an actor control, an int and optional values and prints the text to the client log with the prefix <debug>: instead of returning it. It pushes no value.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071BB80, resolves it with 0x00CC73B0 and reads cell 1 as an int. The argument list builder is 0x0073D460 and the return list builder 0x0072B440.

It allocates 8 bytes and constructs a listener with 0x00713220. The listener vftable is 0x00FD5268 and its RTTI name ends in PrintTextListener. The constructor stores the dword that the engine handle of ExecuteParameters +0x04 addresses at +0x04.

It loads the Y +0x0DC object of the world object, collects the cells from index 2 on with 0x007702C0 and calls 0x00771C20 on the object with the ExecuteParameters pointer, the control handle, the int, the list and the listener.
Slot 1 of the listener vftable is 0x0071C5F0. It builds the literal <debug>: at 0x00FD5C58 and hands the text to the log sink with the kind 0x1F, as recorded for the scheduler contract.

0x00771C20 formats the text and calls the listener with the result, or with the empty string when no text exists. The two call sites of the listener slot are in the bytes, the condition that selects them was not traced.
The shipped scripts contain 4 call sites, all in system/debug_utility. system/debug_u has no descriptor for the name.
All 4 sites are debug:_printText(...) calls on the global debug object with an open list of values and no result used (local scan).
Whether the call can suspend, the text lookup and the case where the listener is called later through the list that 0x00778490 extends.

rows.behavior: Takes two Utf8Strings, tests whether the Lua class named by the first has a function member named by the second, and pushes a float 0.0 and an int 0 on both outcomes. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The body reads cell 0 and cell 1 through 0x0071CE70 and calls 0x00CC8890 with both strings. The return list builder 0x0072BFC0 declares a float and an int and the argument list builder 0x0072BEC0 two Utf8Strings.

0x00CC8890 calls 0x00CD9C80, which resolves the class table by name through 0x00CD8870, pushes the class table, pushes the member name and tests the member with the function test 0x00CF37C0. It returns the test result and 0x00CC8890 stores three dwords that are all 0 on success and all 0xFFFFFFFF on failure.

The failure branch pushes 0.0 through 0x007489D0 and 0 through 0x00584F70. The success branch rebuilds the unsigned qword of the first two stored dwords, which are 0, divides it by 1000000.0 and pushes the float, then pushes the third stored dword, which is 0. Both branches therefore push 0.0 and 0.

The function test follows the stack helper names recorded by the global contract for 0x00CF37C0. The roles of the other stack helpers 0x00CF34C0, 0x00CF3340, 0x00CF3380 and 0x00CF3460 are taken from their call order.
The index lists the name once, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for it.
The site is a string constant. No script calls the name as a method (local scan).
The native name suggests a timing result. No timing source is read, and the success branch divides a zero qword.

rows.behavior: Takes a chara control and pushes the byte that the object chain behind chara +0x0F8 reports, as an int, or Nil when that chain has no object. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the CharaBase cast reader 0x0071BC90 and loads the dword at chara +0x0F8. The return list builder is 0x00728C20 and the argument list builder 0x0072C260.
0x00892FE0 tests the dword at +0x08 of that object. When it is 0 the callback pushes Nil through 0x00748920.

Otherwise 0x006E1160 loads the same +0x0F8 dword again, passes a byte out slot to 0x00893920, which loads the dword at +0x08 and calls 0x00892530, and that routine calls virtual slot 8 (offset 0x20) of the object at +0x04 of its argument. The byte is zero extended and pushed through 0x00584F70.

The byte is an event priority and the +0x0F8 object is the policy manager that the command and talk contracts record at the MyPlayer +0x0F8 slot. The role comes from the native name and the shared offset.
The index lists the name once, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for it.
The site is a string constant. No script calls the name as a method (local scan).
The class of the object at +0x04, the body of virtual slot 8 and the value for a chara that is not a MyPlayer.

arguments.note: Chara control cast to CharaBase, resolved to an identity through 0x00CC73B0.

rows.behavior: Takes a chara control and pushes the Utf8String at +0xB3C of the chara record that its identity names. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071BC90 and resolves it to an identity with 0x00CC73B0. It takes the world object through 0x00CC7510 and calls 0x0075C850 with the identity.

0x0075C850 finds the chara record through the identity registry search 0x004D9970, loads the first dword of the Utf8String at record +0xB3C through 0x00445210 and builds a new Utf8String from that character pointer with 0x00447260. The callback pushes it through 0x007487C0.
The string names a place, which the native name suggests. The bytes state the offset and the copy.
The index lists 1 call site, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for the name.
The site is a debug:_getCharacterLocation(actor) call on the global debug object with one argument, returning the result (local scan).
The writers of the string at +0xB3C and the run time result for an identity that is absent from the registry, because no instruction tests the registry result.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and pushes the control that the first match in the container at Y +0x104 holds, or a null control when nothing matches. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback takes the world object through 0x00CC7510, loads the dword at Y +0x104 and calls 0x007657B0 on it. The return list builder is 0x0072C260 and the argument list builder 0x0072B440.

0x007657B0 searches the node list of the container with the predicate 0x007768E0 through 0x00779CA0 and returns the dword at node +0x08, or 0 when the search reaches the end. The callback pushes the result through 0x00748B30.
The container holds the actors of playing cut scenes, which the native name states. The node layout and the predicate were not traced.
The index lists 1 call site, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for the name.
The site is a debug:_getPlayingCutSceneActor() call on the global debug object with no argument and one result (local scan).
The writers of the container, the predicate and whether a null control is pushed as Nil or as a control cell.

rows.behavior: Takes a quest control and calls virtual slot 29 (offset 0x74) of the QuestBase object with the engine handle. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the QuestBase cast reader 0x0071BF70, loads the engine handle from ExecuteParameters +0x04 and jumps to the slot at offset 0x74 of the object vftable.

Cell 0x00FDFE50 of the QuestBase vftable 0x00FDFDDC holds 0x006DBEA0. That routine calls 0x00CC7370 on its argument with the object, and 0x00CC7370 looks the control state up through 0x00CD7A30 and calls 0x00CDAEB0.
The call removes the quest control from the engine, as the native name says. The bytes show a state lookup and a call to the routine that the catalog names the null binding register.
The Lua name and the registered name occur in no script of the installed client. The index lists no reference, so the native is engine only.
The effect of 0x00CDAEB0 on the control and whether other classes override slot 29.

rows.behavior: Takes a Utf8String and places it on the Windows clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The body reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and converts the string to a UTF-16 string with 0x00449000.
It calls GlobalAlloc with the flag 2 and the size of the converted length times 2 plus 2, locks the block, copies the characters including the terminator through 0x009D4600 and unlocks the block.
It then calls OpenClipboard with a null window, EmptyClipboard, SetClipboardData with the format 0x0D, which is CF_UNICODETEXT, and CloseClipboard. No return value of these calls is tested.

The index lists 1 call site, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for the name. The import slots resolve to GlobalAlloc, GlobalLock and GlobalUnlock in KERNEL32.dll and OpenClipboard, EmptyClipboard, SetClipboardData and CloseClipboard in USER32.dll.
The site is a debug:_copyClipboard(text) call on the global debug object with one argument and no result (local scan).
The conversion rules of 0x00449000 for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.

returns.note: An empty array. Only the count 0 is pushed.

rows.behavior: Takes a SpreadSheet control and pushes the int 0 as the element count of an empty IntegerArray. The routine that should fill the array only clears it, so the result is always empty. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the SpreadSheet cast reader 0x0071C080 and calls 0x006F0F10 on the sheet with an out vector and the engine handle. The return list builder is 0x0072BBF0, entry 12, and the argument list builder 0x0072C260.
0x006F0F10 stores 0 at +0x04, +0x08 and +0x0C of the out vector and returns. It reads nothing from the sheet.
The callback pushes the count, which is 0 for an empty vector, through 0x00584F70. The loop over the elements does not run.
The index lists the name once, in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for it.
The site is a string constant. No script calls the name as a method (local scan).
The native name suggests that it lists attribute numbers of the sheet. The routine that should do so only clears the vector.

rows.behavior: Takes a SpreadSheet control and an int, reads both and pushes false. The result does not depend on either argument. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x0071C080 and cell 1 through 0x005819A0, each after a size test. The return list builder is 0x00728B70 and the argument list builder 0x0072C050.
It stores the byte 0 in the result slot and pushes it through the bool pusher 0x00748870. No instruction between the reads and the push tests either value.
The index lists the name 4 times, all in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u has no descriptor for it.
All 4 sites are string constants. No script calls the name as a method (local scan).
The native name suggests that it tests an attribute of the sheet. Every call answers false.

rows.behavior: Takes a chara control and pushes one list object that holds an entry for every item key of every package of the chara. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through the CharaBase cast reader 0x0071BC90 and calls 0x006F51A0 on it, the item package manager at chara +0xD8 (owner +0xD8 in the item contracts). 0x006EF630 fills a dword vector from the manager. The return list builder is 0x0072C1B0, registry entry 11.

It reserves 0x1000 elements in a second vector through 0x007222D0. For each element of the first vector it calls 0x006EF3F0 to fill a third dword vector and appends it with 0x007208E0, passing the control.
It allocates 0x8C bytes, constructs the list object from the second vector with 0x007252B0 and pushes it through the control pusher 0x00748B30.

The first vector holds package keys and the third vector holds the item keys of one package. The list object is a many tentative control array, which is the type of the return list entry. The meaning of each element was not traced.
The index lists the name 4 times, all in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. system/debug_u assigns the descriptor _getAllItem_inl.
All 4 sites are string constants. No script calls the name as a method (local scan).
The layout of the elements, the bodies of 0x006EF630, 0x006EF3F0 and 0x007208E0 and whether the call can create virtual items.

returns.note: An integer from the lower bound to the upper bound.

rows.behavior: Reads two ints lo and hi and a seed. It steps the seed with the linear step of _randomInteger and pushes lo plus the floor of r over 32768 times hi minus lo plus 1, then pushes the stepped seed. The receiver state at Math +0x64 is not touched. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the inert helper 0x0078BEB0, calls the body 0x0078D270 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and destroys the helper through 0x0078BEC0. The body takes no receiver state.
The body reads cells 0, 1 and 2 through the int reader 0x005819A0, each with its own size test.

The seed step is seed times 0x41C64E6D plus 0x3039 in 32 bits. r is that value shifted right arithmetically by 16 and masked with 0x7FFF. The remaining arithmetic is the one recorded for _randomInteger, with the double -3.0517578125e-05 at 0x00FE0578 and 32 bit float stores.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order.

Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time. The decoded scripts and the call shapes are not redistributed.

The registered key of a native is its name followed by _cpp. The Debug natives that no descriptor targets are called by scripts under the plain name. Whether a lookup path joins that plain name to the registered closure was not traced. A call of a name that resolves to nothing is expected to be the standard Lua 5.1 call of a nil value (INFERRED).

The bodies of the predicates of _getAllCharacter, of the text module routines 0x00773B00 and 0x00771C20, of 0x006FCB80 behind the prog selector of _commandDebug and of the group record routines were not traced.
_getTimeCost, _getSpreadSheetAllAttribute and _isSpreadSheetExistAttribute are constant in the 1.23b client. A client that mirrors them should not compute a value that the bytes do not produce.
The scene packets 0x39 and 0x3A that _setPos and _setDir post are named by the scene record choke point record. Their consumers were not traced here.
